title: Year four close: the many rooms
hook: thinkers, prayers, ethics, hope and the hardest questions: one house with many rooms (John 14:2)
tomorrow: Four women in the family tree (Matthew 1:1–17)

segments.voice: Yesterday, faith as faithfulness: Daniel at his open window, praying as he did aforetime. Your line was keep showing up. What did you come back to? Day one thousand four hundred twenty-six.

At the table on Jesus' last night, one of his friends admits he's lost. Jesus has just told them not to be troubled, and that he is going to prepare a place for them. Thomas doesn't nod along. He says, plainly: "Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?" This year opened with the promise Thomas was answering, about a house with many rooms. Today the year closes in the same room, with the same line, and with Thomas's question still on the table. Today's word: year four close.

Here's the line again, from John's Gospel, in the King James: "In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you." This year walked through that house one room at a time. The big questions, where each church answered in its own voice. Prayer, from the Jesus Prayer to Quaker silence to a hymn. Ethics: commandments, virtues and mercy. The great thinkers, arguing across the centuries. Revelation and Christian hope, from a garden to a garden-city. Church life: rites and spaces, bells and bread. And these last weeks, the hardest room: suffering, doubt, grief, and love that walks into pain without explaining it. Now notice who first heard "many mansions." Not people who had it figured out. Friends who were frightened. Peter, who had just been told he would deny Jesus before the rooster crowed. Thomas, who said out loud that he didn't know the way. Right after Peter hears that, Jesus says: "Let not your heart be troubled." And then: "I go to prepare a place for you." A place is prepared for them as they are, troubled, unsure, about to fail. Christians read the line in more than one way: some hear it about heaven, some about the church on earth, some about life with God that starts now. Some readers hold those side by side. But in the story itself, the promise of a room comes before the confusion is cleared up, not after. Thomas asks his question, and the next thing he hears is an answer, not a rebuke.
screen: `THE YEAR, ONE ROOM AT A TIME.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: write what room you live in. Settle, and breathe. Walk back through the year's rooms in your mind. The room of big questions. The prayer room. The room of ethics. The thinkers' room. The room of hope. The room of bread and bells. The room of hard questions. Which one did you keep returning to? Which one are you standing in today? It might be the room of doubt, with Thomas. That's a room in the house, too. When the bell ends, write one line, starting: I live in the room of... and finish it yourself. If you pray, you can offer that line to God as it is. The bell holds the time.
Year four close. The last day of a year spent in one house with many rooms: thinkers, prayer, ethics, hope and the hardest questions. A house first promised to friends who were afraid.

Your line: there is room for you. Keep your one line somewhere safe. Tomorrow, year five begins: the sources, and living it, starting at the first page of Matthew, with four women in a family tree. Day one thousand four hundred twenty-six.

fork.setup: you're Thomas, at the table. Jesus has just said he's going to prepare a place for you, and that you know the way. you don't. what do you do?
options: say plainly that you don't know where he's going.
fork.reveal: Thomas says: Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way? and what he gets back is an answer, not a rebuke.

original.note: Greek: a dwelling place, a room to stay in. the word behind many mansions in John 14:2.

trapdoor: what you thought: many mansions means grand houses in heaven.
what it means: dwelling places in one house, promised on the last night to friends who were frightened and unsure.
what a scholar hears: monai, rooms to stay in. Christians read the promise as heaven, as the church, or as life with God now, and the room is offered before Thomas's question is cleared up.
recall: Catholic and Orthodox word for it
